newsitem.title: USA: DNC lays off controversial fundraiser Huang.
newsitem.headline: DNC lays off controversial fundraiser Huang.

text.p: The Democratic National Committee has laid off fundraiser John Huang, who solicited several controversial campaign contributions from foreign interests, the Washington Post reported on Monday.
The paper quoted Amy Weiss Tobe saying Huang was among 50 DNC employees let go on Friday as the election season wound down, and that the decision was not due to the controversy surrounding Huang.
She also told the paper that the DNC was returning another $5,000 raised at fundraiser at a Buddhist temple in April, a venue the party now says was inappropriate for a fundraiser.

Huang, a former Commerce Department official, had been the DNC's finance vice chairman since December 1995 and raised $2.5 million for the party. He was relieved of his fundraising duties but continued to draw a salary after reports on problems with the contributions he solicited.
The party has returned nearly $600,000 raised by Huang, including $25,000 that came from a foreign company rather than its U.S. subsidiary.
The contributions prompted Republicans to accuse foreign interests of seeking influence with the White House, and spurred internal investigations by the Commerce Department and the DNC.
